Subject: ACME POC: integration plan & success criteria

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Great to speak earlier today. Recapping our discussion and next steps so we have alignment heading into the POC. Thanks for sharing your primary goals — this writeup is focused on integration scope, success criteria, evaluation plan, ownership, and a suggested timeline.

POC objective:
- Verify that Redwood can serve low-latency, production-grade inference for ACME search enrichment workflows (real-time user queries + tool calling to internal product database).

Success criteria (proposed):
1) Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 350ms on your representative query set (avg token length ~120).
2) Cost: per-query token cost within 30% of current baseline using Redwood batching/quantization recommendations.
3) Functional: tool calling reliability >= 99% for calls to product-db API (idempotent).
4) Quality: pass your 25-case manual prompt set with <= 10% unacceptable responses as judged by your SMEs.

Evaluation plan:
- Week 0: sandbox keys and sample dataset ingestion (you provide 500 representative queries + product-db schema).
- Week 1-2: integration (server-side SDK + streaming enabled).
- Week 3: run evaluation suite (latency/cost/quality), collect logs and traces, iterate.
- Week 4: review and go/no-go meeting.

Owners:
- ACME: Samir Kapoor (Eng lead) — integration and test harness
- ACME: Priya Shah — product acceptance and quality reviewers
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (AE) — program lead; Rafael Mendes (Solutions Eng) — technical owner; Vivek Kulkarni — infra/ops touchpoint

Integration highlights / asks for Samir's team:
- Preferred SDK: Python (server-side) and Node for any edge glue.
- Streaming: we recommend server-side streaming (chunked HTTP / SSE) for low-latency UX.
- Tool calling: Redwood supports typed function_call-style operations (JSON schema) — we can map calls to your product-db endpoints.
- Authentication: sandbox API keys will be issued; production will use mTLS/KMS options if required.

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan-v1.pdf (detailed plan), data-processing-diagram.png, redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx

Next steps:
1) Samir — confirm engineering owner and sandbox environment details by EOD Mon (2026-07-26).
2) ACME — share sample query set and product-db schema (S3/Drive link) by Mon.
3) Redwood — we’ll provision sandbox keys and calendar the kickoff for Tue 7/27 10am PT if that works.

Thanks — happy to adjust any of the items above.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Subject: ACME POC: integration details (SDK, API routes, streaming, tool calling)

Hi Jordan / Samir —

Thanks — answering Samir/Jordan’s questions and adding the concrete integration details Rafael promised on the call:

SDKs and samples:
- Python SDK (recommended for server-side): pip install redwood-sdk
- Node SDK (optional): npm i @redwood/inference
- We’ve attached integration-snippets.zip with sample Python/Node snippets for streaming, retries, and function_call handling.

Core API routes (sandbox):
- POST https://sandbox.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate  -- synchronous generation (JSON).
- POST https://sandbox.api.redwood.ai/v1/stream    -- server-side streaming (SSE / chunked) for incremental tokens.
- POST https://sandbox.api.redwood.ai/v1/call      -- tool-calling webhook flow for calls that require ACME-side resolution.

Streaming notes:
- We support chunked HTTP streaming and SSE. Each chunk contains token/role/meta. Reconnect: resume token offset is supported for transient disconnects.
- Max connection duration: 5 minutes; we recommend heartbeat pings from client if you expect long-lived sessions.

Tool calling (function schema):
- Redwood accepts a JSON schema for each callable action. During a call, Redwood emits a POST to your configured endpoint with {call_id, function_name, args}. Your service returns {call_id, status, result}.
- Calls are retried (idempotent) up to 3x by default; we can adjust per-call settings.

Auth & networking:
- Sandbox: API key (x-api-key) in header.
- Production options: KMS-backed keys + mutual TLS (mTLS) if ACME requires client certs.
- If you have egress limits, provide IP allowlist; we’ll provide the sandbox IP ranges.

Operational hooks:
- Trace IDs are passed in X-Request-ID; logs and token-level cost breakdowns will be available in Redwood Console for the POC.

Proposed timeline (calendar):
- Mon 7/27: Kickoff + provisioning (10am PT).
- 7/27-8/10: Integration window (two weeks).
- Week of 8/10: Run evaluation suite; submit results by 8/14.
- 8/17: Review meeting and next steps.

Action items for Samir's team:
1) Confirm whether sandbox egress needs IP allowlist / mTLS by EOD Mon (2026-07-26).
2) Provide Drive link with sample queries and product-db schema.
3) Confirm preferred SDK (Python or Node).

I’ve attached integration-snippets.zip with a sample curl for streaming and a small python example that calls /v1/stream and shows reconnect logic. Rafael will pulse in on the infra/network questions if needed.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Marissa — thanks for the details. A few technical questions from infra/eng: 

1) Streaming reconnects: can the resume token offset be trusted across restarts, or is it best-effort? What happens if we see duplicate tokens on reconnect?
2) Max sequence length / token limits: do you allow dynamic context window sizing per request? We have some documents up to ~8k tokens; not all queries need that full context.
3) Tool calling: is the call synchronous (i.e., Redwood waits for your endpoint response) or does it support async callback? We prefer async if the product-db lookup can take >2s.
4) CORS / browser use: we will do server-side calls but want to confirm CORS headers for any browser-based debugging UIs.

Also, ACME requires that sandbox egress be restricted to a small IP set; please send over the sandbox IP ranges and certificate info (if you support mTLS).

Samir Kapoor
Staff Eng — ACME Corp

Hi Samir / Jordan —

Thanks for the detailed questions — Rafael and I discussed internally and here are the short answers and actions so we don’t block your timeline: 

1) Streaming resume semantics: resume token offset is best-effort and works for transient disconnects. Small duplicate tokens may occur on reconnect; clients should de-duplicate on token id. Sample client code in integration-snippets.zip shows safe dedupe.
2) Context window: we support up to 16k tokens per request in the sandbox; you can set the context length per request. For very long docs we recommend chunking + retrieval.
3) Tool calling: both sync and async flows are supported. If you expect >2s processing, use async callback mode — Redwood will surface call_id and await your /call/result endpoint.
4) CORS: server-side recommended; sandbox endpoints will include permissive CORS headers for debugging and we’ll lock them down for production.
5) Networking / mTLS: attaching our sandbox IP ranges and mTLS FAQ (see links). If you need mTLS, we can provision client certs for POC.

Action items (next 48 hours):
- Redwood: provision sandbox API key + send IP ranges + attach mTLS cert steps (Rafael taking point).
- ACME: upload sample queries + schema to the Drive folder and confirm Samir’s preferred SDK (Python) by tomorrow.
- Schedule kickoff: Tue 7/27 10am PT — calendar invite (https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=acme-poc-kickoff-20260727) sent to attendees.

We’ll also post a short README in the Drive folder with the sample curl for /v1/stream and the Node/Python snippets. Looking forward to getting started.

Best,
